label: Daylight saving time, time zones and daylight hours

source.reflectsPeriod: 2025-2026 rules (no dated instances; rules are stable across years)
source.basis: US Code 5 USC 6103 (federal holidays), NIST/US DOT daylight-saving rules (Uniform Time Act as amended 2005), typical K-12 and college academic calendars from state/district and university catalogs as recalled, BLS National Compensation Survey for paid-holiday prevalence, FLSA and FMCSA hours rules.

start.doc: {rule, local_time, effect} of the spring-forward change.

end.doc: {rule, local_time, effect} of the fall-back change.

exceptions.doc: Places that do not observe DST.

standard_offsets_h.doc: IANA zone to its standard-time UTC offset in hours; add 1 during DST except Phoenix and Honolulu.

daylight_hours.doc: The source's `daylight_hours_geometric`: {note, rows by latitude with *_h day lengths at the solstices and equinox}.

start.effect: clocks jump to 03:00 (spring forward, lose an hour)

end.effect: clocks fall back to 01:00 (gain an hour)

exceptions: Arizona (except the Navajo Nation) does not observe DST
Territories (Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, Northern Marianas) do not observe DST
us.note: Offsets listed are standard time; during DST add +1 hour except Phoenix and Honolulu. Congress has not enacted permanent DST (as of the basis date).

daylight_hours.note: Geometric day length (sunrise to sunset, no atmospheric refraction; add about 8-10 minutes in practice) by latitude at the solstices and equinox. Use for seasonal light cycles.
